questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: The doctor said to me, “You should not skip meals.”
opts: The doctor said me not to skip meals.
The doctor advised me that not skip meals.
The doctor advised me not to skip meals.
The doctor told me should not skip meals.
questions.why: 'Should' advice is reported with 'advised ... (not) to'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct preposition: “The athlete broke his own record by jumping ____ a five-feet-high bar.”
questions.why: One jumps over a bar. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: In the sentence “Unless you work hard, you will fail,” the clause “Unless you work hard” is a:
questions.why: 'Unless' means 'if not' and introduces a condition. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “By the time I reached the station, the train ____ already.”
questions.why: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “By the time the ambulance arrived, the patient ______ consciousness.”
questions.why: An earlier past action before another past action takes the past perfect. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: “Nobody called, ____?”
questions.why: 'Nobody' is negative, so the tag is positive; it takes 'they'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “I saw her yesterday.”
opts: He said that he saw her yesterday.
He said that he had seen her the day before.
He said that he had seen her yesterday.
He says that he had seen her the day before.
questions.why: Past simple becomes past perfect; 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “She said that she ____ the report the previous day.”
questions.why: In reported speech a past time reference shifts to the past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.
